abstract: BACKGROUND: Osteogenic protein-1 (OP-1) is a member of the transforming growth factor-beta super family closely related to the bone morphogenetic proteins and also known as bone morphogenetic protein-7. Other members of this family of growth factors influence cell differentiation as well as cell growth in a number of systems. The Drosophila homolog encoded by the decapentaplegic locus is involved in dorsal-ventral pattern formation during embryogenesis, whereas the expression of several bone morphogenetic proteins including OP-1 is developmentally regulated in mammalian embryos. EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: The effect of recombinant human OP-1 on the proliferation and differentiation of an established pluripotent human embryonal carcinoma (EC) cell line, NTERA2, and three nullipotent human EC cell lines, 2102Ep, 833KE and TERA-1, was investigated. These cells were grown under reduced serum conditions, and differentiation was monitored by morphology and expression of marker antigens. RESULTS: OP-1 inhibited proliferation of NTERA2 and induced their differentiation, marked by changes in cellular morphology, the loss of EC cell antigens (SSEA3, SSEA4, the liver isozyme of alkaline phosphatase), and the appearance of new antigens, notably SSEA1 and class 1 major histocompatibility complex antigens. These changes were irreversible and did not involve significant cell degeneration or cell death. The OP-1-induced differentiation of NTERA2 appeared distinct from that induced by either retinoic acid or hexamethylene bisacetamide. Nevertheless, OP-1 did induce the homeobox gene, HOXA1. By contrast, OP-1 elicited only a limited and partial response from the nullipotent EC cell lines. CONCLUSIONS: Our results suggest that pluripotent human EC cells differentiate in response to OP-1 and that this factor can modulate the differentiation induced by retinoic acid. Like other members of the transforming growth factor-beta super family, OP-1 might play an inductive role in the early embryo. The results also suggest a possible therapeutic value for OP-1 in the treatment of some germ cell tumors.
abstract_ja: 背景：骨形成タンパク質-1(OP-1)は、形質転換増殖因子β(TGF-β)スーパーファミリーに属し、骨形成タンパク質(BMP)と近縁で、骨形成タンパク質-7(BMP-7)としても知られる。このファミリーの他の成員は、多くの系において細胞の増殖だけでなく分化にも影響を与える。ショウジョウバエの相同遺伝子decapentaplegicは背腹パターン形成に関与し、OP-1を含む数種のBMPの発現は哺乳類胚で発生段階に応じて制御される。実験デザイン：樹立された多能性ヒト胎児性癌(EC)細胞株NTERA2と、3種の非多能性ヒトEC細胞株2102Ep、833KE、TERA-1に対する組換えヒトOP-1の増殖・分化への影響を検討した。細胞は血清を減らした条件で培養し、形態と抗原マーカー発現により分化を評価した。結果：OP-1はNTERA2の増殖を抑制し分化を誘導した。形態変化、EC細胞抗原(SSEA3、SSEA4、肝型アルカリホスファターゼ)の消失、SSEA1とクラスI主要組織適合抗原の出現がみられた。これらの変化は不可逆的で、有意な細胞変性や細胞死は伴わなかった。OP-1によるNTERA2の分化は、レチノイン酸やヘキサメチレンビスアセトアミドによるものとは異なっていた。それでもOP-1はホメオボックス遺伝子HOXA1を誘導した。対照的に、非多能性EC細胞株からは限定的かつ部分的な反応しか得られなかった。結論：多能性ヒトEC細胞はOP-1に応答して分化し、本因子はレチノイン酸による分化を修飾しうる。TGF-βスーパーファミリーの他の成員と同様に、OP-1は初期胚で誘導的役割を果たす可能性がある。また、一部の胚細胞腫瘍の治療におけるOP-1の治療的価値も示唆される。
